title: Count Equal Pairs Within Distance k
statement:
You are given an array `code` of `n` integers and an integer `k`.

Count the unordered pairs of positions `(i, j)` with `i < j` such that `code[i] == code[j]` and `j - i <= k`.

Every pair of positions is counted separately, even if the values repeat many times (for example, three equal neighbours produce three pairs when `k >= 2`).
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers `code[0..n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of valid pairs.
constraints: The answer can exceed 32 bits; use 64-bit integers.

examples.explanation: Valid pairs: (0, 2), (2, 3) and (3, 5). Pairs such as (0, 3) and (1, 4) are three positions apart, which is more than k = 2.
Every one of the C(5, 2) = 10 pairs of positions has distance at most 4.
Equal values are two positions apart but k = 1, so no pair qualifies.

hints: For each position j, count how many earlier positions i in the range [j - k, j - 1] hold the same value.
Keep a hash map from value to its number of occurrences inside the current window of the last k elements.
When the window moves past position j - k - 1, decrement that element's count before counting matches for j.
